title: surge-scenario-kpi-degradation-simulator-sheet
content:
Purpose:
This sheet is a lightweight, scenario-driven simulator for product ops launches that may produce sudden traffic surges. It ties simulated traffic inputs to expected KPI degradation, action triggers, and automated/manual fallback options. Use during launch planning, canary design, and post-launch runbooks to validate SLA commitments and run capacity/pricing experiments.

Scope and assumptions:
- Models: hosted-redwood/default-text-gen-v1 (primary), hosted-redwood/compact-text-v1 (fallback)
- Baseline traffic distribution: 10k requests/day, median tokens/request = 120
- KV/prefix cache hit rate baseline: 18% (can be tuned)
- Autoscaling delay: 90s median to add a GPU pod in Dedicated mode; burst capacity available up to +30% for 2 mins
- Cost assumptions used for simulated cost delta: internal cost-per-token estimate (used for scenario comparison only)

How to use this sheet:
1) Pick a scenario row below (baseline / 2x / 5x / 10x viral).
2) Inspect expected metric deltas and gate triggers.
3) Confirm owners and playbook steps for each trigger.
4) Run smoke tests against canary after enabling each mitigation.

Simulation scenarios (rows represent independent runs):
Scenario | Traffic multiplier | Peak RPS | Expected p50 (ms) | Expected p95 (ms) | Error rate (%) | GPU util (%) | Queue depth (avg) | Cost delta (relative) | Primary risk
Baseline | 1x | 11 RPS | 85 | 220 | 0.2 | 48 | 2 | +0% | N/A
Holiday peak | 2x | 22 RPS | 110 | 320 | 0.6 | 72 | 5 | +18% | p95 drift, autoscale lag
Product mention (viral) | 5x | 55 RPS | 140 | 520 | 2.4 | 95 | 18 | +70% | queueing + rate limit spikes
Uncontrolled burst | 10x | 110 RPS | 210 | 980 | 8.5 | 100 | 60 | +180% | sustained OOMs / model throttles

KPI gating thresholds (automated alarms to wire into Console alerts):
- p95 latency: warn at >400ms, critical at >700ms
- Error rate: warn at >1.0%, critical at >3.0%
- CPU/GPU util (per node): warn at >85%, critical at >98%
- Queue depth: warn at >12 avg, critical at >30 avg
- Cache hit rate: warn if drops >10% absolute from baseline

Mitigation matrix (ordered, pick the highest-lowest friction first):
1) Short-term config flips (30–120s) - Engage owner: "Devops on-call"
   - Increase request timeout vs client (lenient) to reduce tail failures
   - Enable heavier prefix/KV caching for the route via Redwood Optimize suggested cache policy
2) Traffic shaping / client-side backpressure - Owner: "Platform Eng"
   - Apply rate limits per API key to smooth spikes; return 429 with Retry-After when over threshold
3) Autoscale tuning & burst capacity - Owner: "Infra"
   - Temporarily increase burst pool and lower scale-up threshold (aggressive)
4) Model downgrade (fast fallback) - Owner: "Applied ML"
   - Route a % of traffic to compact-text-v1 (lower throughput cost) using the Console rollout (canary -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%)
5) Regional failover - Owner: "Site Reliability Engineering"
   - Re-route traffic to alternate region with available capacity (legal/latency constraints considered)
6) Emergency: soft fail to degraded feature mode - Owner: "Product Ops"
   - Disable non-critical SSE/streaming or tool-calls to save tokens and throughput

Runbook: step-by-step for critical alarm (p95 >700ms OR error rate >3% sustained for 3m)
- T0 (alert received): Triage and confirm alert fidelity (owner: on-call SRE, channel: #prod-alerts).
- T0+2m: Check Console dashboard: per-route token breakdown, top-10 request signatures, cache hit rate, model allocation.
- T0+3m: Enable 10% fallback to compact-text-v1 via console rollout. Run synthetic smoke test (owner: applied-ml).
- T0+6m: If metrics improve (>30% p95 reduction), continue ramp to 50% and monitor.
- T0+10m: If still critical, enable autoscale burst and spin additional Dedicated capacity. Inform CS + Sales of potential degradations.
- T0+30m: If unresolved, initiate regional failover or enable degraded-mode per product policy. Communicate externally per incident comms playbook.

Acceptance checklist before traffic ramp to 2x baseline (canary stage):
- [ ] Canary route created and traffic split automation validated (owner: product-ops)
- [ ] Automated dashboards and alerts deployed for p50/p95/errors/queue/cache (owner: observability)
- [ ] Canary synthetic harness run with 1000 samples and baseline p95 within +20% of expected (owner: developer-experience)
- [ ] Rollout rollback automation validated (owner: release-engineering)
- [ ] CS and Sales notified of rollout window and escalation contacts (owner: customer-success)

Suggested monitoring queries (examples to paste into Console query editor):
- p95 latency per route (last 5m): quantile_over_time(0.95, latency_ms[5m]) by (route)
- error rate (last 1m): sum(rate(errors_total[1m])) / sum(rate(requests_total[1m]))
- cache hit rate: sum(cache_hits) / (sum(cache_hits) + sum(cache_misses))

Notes on simulation fidelity and tuning: 
- This sheet intentionally simplifies queue dynamics and does not model model-specific kv-cache warmup costs; run a load test on staging for high-confidence numbers.
- Replace cost-delta with actual billing numbers post-launch to calibrate the estimator.
